newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slides 20 cents on NYMEX weakness.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slides 20 cents on NYMEX weakness.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures slid 20 cents a barrel to a new session low on Thursday in reaction to NYMEX crude weakness, before bouncing nine cents to trade 38 cents down on the day, traders said.

"We were just following the TI (West Texas Intermediate) down," a trader said. "New York fell and triggered some stops. Some locals who were short over there (in New York) joined in the selling over here."
April Brent were trading at $20.25 a barrel at 1646 GMT after sliding in 10 minutes to an intraday low of $20.17 from $20.37.
NYMEX crude was down 51 cents at $22.30 on bearish views of ample supply after stock data showed the first year-on-year surplus in three months.
API stock figures released late on Wednesday showed U.S. crude oil inventories rose by 3.12 million barrels last week.
London traders said April Brent had triggered rapid selling after breaking key support at $20.32.
Some traders said Brent would have to regain that level to stand a chance of maintaining a $20.30-20.50 range.
Support was put at $20.10 followed by $20.00.
